nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of W18O49 NWs
nodes.procedure: A mixture of WCl6 (500 mg) and PVP (20 mg) precursors was dissolved in absolute ethanol (50 mL), and a homogeneous yellow solution was obtained after stirring for 30 min. Afterwards, the obtained solutions were transferred into a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave and heated at 180 °C for 24 h. The resultant blue W18O49 product was collected after purification and centrifugation.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of W18O49 NWs... In a typical procedure, a mixture of WCl6 (500 mg) and PVP (20 mg) precursors was dissolved in absolute ethanol (50 mL)... heated at 180 °C for 24 h.

nodes.name: Ni foam pretreatment and W18O49 coating
nodes.procedure: The Ni foam (2 cm × 4 cm) was treated by 0.1 M HCl solutions, and washed with absolute ethanol and distilled water before drying at 60 °C. A total of 50 mg W18O49 powder was re-dispersed into 2 mL ethanol by sonication, and the homogeneous ink was dropped onto the pre-treated Ni foam (2 cm × 4 cm). Ni foam supported W18O49 powder was pressed into a thinner foil structure.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of W18O49@Ni foam section in Methods.

nodes.name: Organic coating with PDA precursors
nodes.procedure: The fabricated W18O49@Ni foam was immersed into mixture solutions (250 mL) of DA (100 mg), P123 (160 mg), and Tris (40 mg), and W18O49@PDA@Ni foam was obtained after stirring for 24 h. In addition, W18O49 powder was also added into the same mixture solutions containing DA, P123, and Tris components with continuous stirring for 24 h.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of W18O49@PDA@Ni foam section in Methods.

nodes.name: Pyrolysis-reduction of W/WO2
nodes.procedure: The desired W/WO2 metallic heterostructure was obtained by pyrolyzing the W18O49@PDA@Ni foam precursor at 700 °C under a mixture of Ar/H2 (v/v = 8:1) atmosphere for 2 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: W/WO2 shows hybrid signals of WO2 monoclinic phase (25.8°, 37.1°, 52.9°, 59.7° for (011), (−211), (220), (031)) and metallic W simple cubic phase (a=b=c=3.16 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure of W/WO2 heterostructure was verified by X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern. As shown in Supplementary Fig. 4, besides of the predominant characteristics of underlying Ni foam, the XRD pattern of WO2 sample reveals a set of characteristic signals at 25.8°, 37.1°, 52.9°, and 59.7°, which are indexed to the (011), (−211), (220), and (031) facets of monoclinic structured WO2 phase (JCPDS No. 32–1393), respectively, while metallic W NPs present a simple cubic phase with lattice parameters of a = b = c = 3.16 Å (JCPDS no. 89–2767).

nodes.characterization_summary: W/WO2 shows 1D nanorod structure with radial lengths over 500 nm coating Ni foam skeletons.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From low-magnification SEM image, the Ni skeletons are closely coated by W/WO2 products (Supplementary Fig. 5a, b), and the high-magnification SEM image and corresponding energy dispersive X-ray spectra (EDS) show one-dimensional (1D) nanorod structure of the as-obtained W/WO2 materials with radial lengths over 500 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: High density W nanoparticles <10 nm dispersed on WO2 nanorods with lattice fringes of 0.22 nm (W (110)) and 0.34 nm (WO2 (011)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) can allow us to observe the hybrid structure of W/WO2 metallic heterostructure at atomic level. As shown in Fig. 1a, high density of nanoparticles with sizes less than 10 nm are dispersed on tungsten-based nanorods, and two sets of lattice fringes with spacing values of 0.22 and 0.34 nm can be seen from the high-magnification STEM image (Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous distribution of C (blue), O (red), and W (green) elements over entire W/WO2 heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the homogeneous distribution of C, O, and W elements over the entire W/WO2 metallic heterostructure is visualized by the STEM-EDS mapping images (Fig. 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: W/WO2 shows coexistence of W⁰ (31.4 eV 4f7/2, 33.5 eV 4f5/2) and W⁴⁺ (32.7 eV 4f7/2, 34.8 eV 4f5/2) with surface W⁶⁺ oxidation species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a, W and WO2 samples exhibit W⁰ and W⁴⁺ signals at low (31.4 eV for W⁰ 4f7/2 and 33.5 eV for W⁰ 4f5/2) and high (32.7 eV for W⁴⁺ 4f7/2 and 34.8 eV for W⁴⁺ 4f5/2) binding energies after deconvolution, respectively... As expected, W/WO2 sample contains features of both W and WO2 species at the same binding energies after deconvolution.

nodes.characterization_summary: W L3-edge XANES of W/WO2 shows white line intensity between W (lowest) and WO2 (highest), indicating average W oxidation state between 0 and +4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The normalized X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) profiles of W L3-edge reveal that the white line intensity of W/WO2 sample is much higher than that of metallic W NPs, but slightly lower relative to that of WO2 counterpart (Fig. 2b), indicating the average oxidation state of tungsten atoms in W/WO2 is between 0 and 4+.

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge NEXAFS shows W/WO2 has decreased W-O bonds (530.7 eV) but increased superoxide O₂⁻ species (532.2 eV) vs WO2, indicating rich oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: One can see that both WO2 and W/WO2 samples exhibit split peaks located at energies ranging from 530 to 535 eV, where the peak at low energy (530.7 eV) originates from the overlapping band between W5d and O 2p orbitals... Comparing to the O K-edge NEXAFS spectroscopy of W counterpart, W/WO2 metallic heterostructure exhibits decreased intensity of W-O bonds but increased signal of O₂⁻ species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Strong symmetrical ESR signal at g=2.002 manifests rich unpaired electrons trapped on oxygen vacancies around W centers in W/WO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, such an enrichment of oxygen vacancies in W/WO2 metallic heterostructure is also resolved by electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy (Supplementary Fig. 7), which exhibits a strong and symmetrical ESR signal at g = 2.002, manifesting rich unpaired electrons trapped on vacancies around W centers.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS R-space shows W/WO2 combines W-W scattering (2.6 Å) and W-O coordination (1.6 Å) features with enhanced metallic W-W path vs pure WO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As can be seen, W sample exhibits a distinct peak at 2.6 Å, corresponding to the W-W scattering path, while a predominant peak at approximately 1.6 Å is presented on WO2 sample... As expected, the R-space profile of W/WO2 heterostructure exhibits the combined features of W and WO2 counterparts.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl of W/WO2 is 87.5 mF/cm², 3.7-fold and 2.1-fold higher than W and WO2 respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl value of W/WO2 catalyst is determined to be up to 87.5 mF/cm², nearly 3.7- and 2.1-fold enhancement than those of W and WO2 counterparts, respectively (Fig. 3e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows R2 decreases to 4.4 Ω at -20 mV and R3 to 1.8 Ω with CΦ=0.017 F at -30 mV for W/WO2, indicating fast charge transfer and low H adsorption resistance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In particular, R2 decreases to 4.4 Ω sharply with a negligible water diffusion resistance at applied overpotential of -20 mV... the value of R3 can be as low as approximately 1.8 Ω, while CΦ is up to 0.017 F at an overpotential of -30 mV.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows dissolved W concentrations of 7.5×10⁻⁶ (initial), 9.8×10⁻⁶ (used), 6.3×10⁻⁷ mol/L (refreshed) after long-term HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After long-term hydrogen production, the initial electrolyte, used electrolyte, and refreshed electrolyte (indicated by red dashed circle) shows no significant increase in the concentrations of dissolved W species with values of 7.5×10⁻⁶, 9.8×10⁻⁶, and 6.3×10⁻⁷ mol/L, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms W content of 79.1 wt% in W/WO2 materials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The loading mass of tungsten element was 3.2 mg/cm² in accordance with the ICP-MS analysis (W: 79.1 wt%).

nodes.characterization_summary: Under 0.1 mbar H2O, W/WO2 shows vanished Ov signal but enhanced W-OH (532.3 eV) and H2O (533.3 eV) with decreased low-valence W species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After introducing 0.1 mbar H2O molecules... W/WO2 metallic heterostructure exhibits a vanished 0v signal but significantly enhanced concentrations of W-OH (532.3 eV) and H2O (533.3 eV) species... indicating Ov have served as the adsorption sites of H2O molecules, and the cleavage of H-OH bonds is easily proceeded.

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS shows sharply increased H3O+ signal (m/z=19.02) on electrochemically treated W/WO2 vs soaked reference, confirming proton-concentrated surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We can observe that the electrochemically treated W/WO2 catalyst exhibits markedly increased signals of hydrogen-containing intermediates... in particular, the sharply increased H3O+ signal directly suggests the formation of proton-concentrated catalyst surface.

properties.description: Red peak with high intensity at ~17.5 m/z

nodes.characterization_summary: REELS shows gradually enhanced H signals on electrochemically treated W/WO2 (0 to -30 mV) vs soaked sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As expected, all electrochemically treated W/WO2 catalysts exhibited gradually enhanced H signals when increasing the applied overpotentials (0 to -30 mV), indicating a proton-concentrated surface could be constructed.

nodes.characterization_summary: 1H MAS NMR shows increased W·OH_T (-1.3 ppm) and W·OH_L (3.4 ppm) signals with decreasing W-OH_T/W-OH_L ratio under increasing overpotentials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All electrochemically treated W/WO2 samples exhibit significant increased signals of W·OH_T and W·OH_L species under increasing overpotentials... the proportion of W-OH_T/W·OH_L decreases with the increase of applied potentials.

nodes.characterization_summary: Py-IR shows enhanced Brønsted acid sites (1540, 1638 cm⁻¹) with increasing overpotentials on electrochemically treated W/WO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Impressively, the electrochemically treated W/WO2 catalysts also exhibited enhanced concentrations of Brønsted acid sites with the increase of applied overpotentials.
